title: Add the two core-row section errors (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

A second output kept at distance `ceil(p^{48})` inherits the same #4491 reading as the first. The distance comparison does not name a row, so both outputs satisfy `R < p^{26} < A`.

For each output:

- With no gauge, the section-polynomial row is the global polynomial row.
- Under that section's own #4452 gauge, `||P - H_sec^{-1}||_2 < ε` with `ε = p^6 exp(-p^2)`, and the core row is a row of that operator.

On the two matched rows the section polynomials equal the same global row, so

```text
row(B) - row(C) = (row(B) - row(P)) + (row(P) - row(C)).
```

Two positive integers strictly below 4, namely 3 and 3, sum to 6, and `6 < 2 * 4`. A polynomial gap of 2 spends that room: `3 + 2 + 3 = 8`, which is not strictly below 8. One error alone is not the two-error sum.

This is the shared-row sum. It is not the operator norm `||B - C||_2` of the two section inverses, and it is not the global-inverse summand. Both ideal-gap gauges stay hypotheses. One section's gauge does not cover the other. No new κ. The selected record remains `23/10000`.

This answers the open question of #4511 for the two row errors. Whether the sum lifts to the operator hypothesis in #4509 is left open.

## Test plan

- [x] `python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/gaussian-second-row`
- [x] Prints `PASS_GAUSSIAN_SECOND_ROW` and `outcome=completed`
- [ ] Maintainer replay was not run

Base `f9f85c1e4fa1e955ff39f10fca447e3e2a4e4adc`, priority revision 7. Upstream fetched at 2026-10-22T03:04:25Z was that commit, and the pre-submit fetch at 2026-10-22T03:06:24Z was unchanged. κ remains `23/10000`.
